conditions: The statement compares application of a selected template rule and an invocation by the named-template instruction.
limitations: One xsl:template may carry both a name and a match pattern. Rule conflict resolution, modes and error handling have their own clauses.

triggers: W3C source correction or erratum, spec byte drift, or material contrary scoped evidence.

statement: Applying an XSLT 3.0 template rule evaluates the template’s sequence constructor with the matching item as the context item. Invoking a template by name with xsl:call-template leaves the focus unchanged.
